- Certified type: Water meter MA408K
- Module designation: Ultrasonic water meters with electronic indication device

Models: The cert covers DN15, DN20, DN25 variants. So model_family with models DN15, DN20, DN25.

Model-level characteristics:
- Nominal diameter: DN15, DN20, DN25 (mm). Values: 15, 20, 25? Actually the values are "DN15", "DN20", "DN25" — these are designations. I could record nominal_diameter with values "DN15" etc., or numeric 15, 20, 25 with unit mm. I'll use numeric with unit mm.
- Permanent flowrate Q3: 2.5, 4, 6.3 m³/h (decimal commas → convert)
- Minimum flowrate Q1: 0.00625, 0.010, 0.01575 m³/h
- Transitional flowrate Q2: 0.010, 0.016, 0.0252 m³/h
- Overload flowrate Q4: 3.125, 5, 7.875 m³/h
- Connection thread: G ¾ B, G1 B, G1 ¼ B (strings)
- Construction length L: 165, 190/195/165, 225 mm. Hmm, DN20 has "190/195/165" — multiple values. As a string "190/195/165" or list? The schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. I'll keep string "190/195/165". Actually maybe better keep as string.

Note: There's a discrepancy between the dimensions table (DN25: A=260) and the technical data table (Construction length DN25: 225). I'll record both tables.

Type-level characteristics:
- Ratio Q3/Q1: 400 (unit R)
- Ratio Q2/Q1: 1.6 (dimensionless)
- Installation orientation: H/V (string)
- Water temperature range: 0.1 to 50 °C (T50 temperature class). Value {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C. Temperature class T50.
- Maximum admissible pressure MAP: 16 bar
- Pressure loss: 0.40 bar, class Δp 40. Two entries: pressure_loss: {value: 0.4, unit_symbol: "bar"}, pressure_loss_class: {value: "Δp 40"} → canonical label maybe pressure_loss_class value "40"? The table says "0,40" bar and "Δp 40". I'll record pressure_loss: 0.4 bar and pressure_loss_class: "Δp40" as string. Let me use "pressure_loss_class": {"value": "Δp 40", ...}. Hmm, canonical labels — maybe "pressure_loss_class" with value string "Δp 40". Fine.
- Maximum permissible error in upper flowrates range (Q2 ≤ Q ≤ Q4): ±2% (at T ≤ 30°C), ±3% (at T > 30°C). The "Ø" is OCR artifact for T. This is config_level (by temperature condition). Or could be type_level with two entries. I'll use config_level: attribute "maximum_permissible_error_upper_range", axis "water_temperature", values: [{condition: "T ≤ 30°C", value: 2, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "T > 30°C", value: 3, unit_symbol: "%"}].
- MPE lower range (Q1 ≤ Q < Q2): ±5% → value 5? ±5 means -5 to +5. Could be {min: -5, max: 5}? Rules say ± values... For MPE ±2% could be {min: -2, max: 2}. Hmm. I think recording as number with the ± preserved... The schema: value can be number or range. For MPE, I'd use {min: -5, max: 5} to be faithful? Or keep value: 5 and label indicates max permissible error (positive). Typical OIML extraction: value ±5% → value 5 (magnitude). I'll use number 5 with unit "%". Actually to be safe, use value as number (magnitude). Hmm, but the strict structured values say numbers not strings. I'll use magnitude numbers.
- Capacity of calculator: 999999.999 m³
- Scale interval (normal resolution): 0.001 m³
- Scale interval (high resolution): 0.0000001 m³
- Accuracy class: 2
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: -25 to +55 °C → {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C
- Electromagnetic class: E1/E2 (string)
- Climatic and mechanical environmental conditions class per EN ISO 4064-1/OIML R 49-1: B/O (string)
- Flow profile sensitivity class: U0D0
- Battery: non-replaceable li-battery 3.8 V, lifetime 10 years. Characteristics: battery_type: "non-replaceable lithium battery"? battery_nominal_voltage: 3.8 V; battery_life: 10 years. Also from page 3: two non-replaceable lithium batteries, lifetime 10 years, 9 Ah. So battery_quantity: 2? battery_capacity: 9 Ah. Record: battery_nominal_voltage 3.8 V, battery_lifetime 10 years (unit "a" or "years"?). unit_symbol "years"? I'll use "a" (annum)? Safer: "years". unitsdb might have year as "a". Rules say leave unit_id null unless certain; unit_symbol raw is fine. I'll use "years".

- Software version: 2014, checksum D281BE55. Record as type_level characteristic? The schema has no software section; could put in characteristics type_level: software_version: "2014", software_checksum: "D281BE55". Good.
- Display: LCD 9 digits, indication range 999999.999 m³. Covered by capacity of calculator.
- Indication range: 999999.999 m³ — same as capacity.

Matrix tables:
1. Technical and metrological data table (section 5) — could be matrix_tables with columns. I'll emit it as a matrix_table with rows per DN, and also populate model_level.
2. Dimensions table (Fig. 2): columns: designation, a_length, b, c, d_connection_thread, e. Rows: DN15: A 165, B 95.5, C 103.4, D G 3/4, E 185.4; DN20: 190, 95.5, 107.1, G1, 189.1; DN25: 260, 95.5, 109.9, G1 1/4, 191.9. Decimal commas → 95.5 etc.
3. Fig 4a parts list — components list. This is parts list; could include as matrix_tables? It's a BOM. Maybe include as components? The components[] in schema are for named sub-assemblies like "Flow sensor", "Calculator and indication device". The BOM parts are minor. I could include matrix_tables for the assembly parts list but that seems noisy. I'll include the essential components (flow sensor, calculator and indication device, internal valve, strainer, optical port) as components[] with roles. And optionally include Fig 4b assembly parts as a matrix_table? I think skip — too noisy. Actually rule 6 says record components for complex instruments. The water meter essential parts: Flow sensor, Calculator and indication device. Non-essential: internal valve, motor, strainer, optical port. I'll record components for these.

Maybe include the Fig. 4a parts list as matrix_table? It's a parts list, multi-dim. I'd include it to preserve info: name "Exploded view parts list (Fig 4a)", columns: part_number_no, part_description, quantity. Rows for each. Hmm, that's 21 rows. It's optional. I'll include it as a matrix_table to preserve. Actually, the schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The parts list doesn't fit elsewhere. I'll include it, maybe abbreviated but complete is better. Let me include with columns ["item_no", "part_description", "quantity"].

Fig 4b assembly table: item, part number, drawing code, description, material, quantity. I'll include as second matrix_table. Also noisy but preserves data. I'll include both — more complete extraction. Hmm. Let me weigh: output length is fine. I'll include them.

Actually, let me reconsider — the instructions say "preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere". These parts lists fit that. Include.
